rv.q: Harris touches skillfully on the issue of illicit sexual fantasy... but he fails to convince us fully as to why at least two of these pairs might have thought such a high-risk gamble worth taking.
There is undoubtedly a pervading artificiality to the single-lens perspective through which the failures of the biracial relationships being examined are perceived.
The overall acting is a bit hammed, rich in strong, exaggerated movements and fighting scenes choreographed by Jade Hackett.
Slave Play is too obsessed with conceptual naval gazing to the extent that it forgets that its characters are human beings.
It's funny, clever and undoubtedly challenging, though neither as outrageous nor profound as it would like to be.
